note: The single source of truth for every colour value in this packet. A template carries these values inline in a sentinel-marked palette block, and check-corpus.cjs compares the block against this file in both directions. Edit here, then propagate. The values are the evilcharts Style Reference the packet carries beside its forms (assets/style-reference/evilcharts/DESIGN.md): its canvas, ink, ash and rule carry the chrome; its ink, ash and slate carry the neutral system; its flame, teal, violet and rose carry the categorical system, chosen because those four are the hues that clear a mark on both grounds; and flame drawn toward each ground carries the ordered ramp. Two neutral steps were moved by the least amount that clears a gate, and the derivation block below names both.
chromeDarkNote: The ground a reader gets when their operating system asks for dark: the cursor ink itself, which the reference already uses as the surface behind its light action fills. Parchment becomes the ink and mist the muted tone, both clearing the text gate on that ground. The rule is ink at nine percent rather than a solid grey, chosen so the same declaration reads as a hairline on both grounds.

chromeRoles.surface: The page and card ground. Every contrast ratio in this file is measured against it.
chromeRoles.ink: Primary text: the headline and any label a reader has to read exactly.
chromeRoles.muted: Secondary text: the subtitle, the axis labels and the source line.
chromeRoles.rule: Gridlines, axis lines and card borders. Structure, never data.
chromeRoles.separator: Not a value. Shapes that touch are separated by a stroke in surface, so no two data colours ever share an edge.

radiusRoles.ladder: One 2px knob, five steps, on the cursor reference's 4px corner with 8px for the one container that holds a whole card. Every step is a corner the corpus actually draws, so a rung exists for a consumer rather than for symmetry.
radiusRoles.mark: A data mark's corner: a bar end, a box body, a calendar cell, a legend swatch, a ring tick.
radiusRoles.track: A percentage bar and the track it runs inside.
radiusRoles.swatch: A colour block large enough to be read as a panel rather than as a mark.
radiusRoles.pill: A progress track and its fill, which read as one capsule.
radiusRoles.card: The card that holds the chart.
radiusRoles.notALadderRung: A corner computed from a mark's own geometry, such as a range bar rounded to half its width, is geometry rather than a shared value. It stays in the drawing code.

typeScale.note: The chart register and the proof-sheet register, side by side. Not colours, and like the corner ladder they sit in their own object for that reason: they are the other half of the vocabulary a template reads, and they live here so the check that rejects a size off the scale reads a value rather than restating one. The chart roles are the compact card scale measured from the frozen shadcn copy, and the metric rung is the value a card leads with when its data has a meaningful baseline; in-figure text steps down a rung as a form gets denser, which is the scale working.
typeScale.departureNote: Each departure below is a single number that is the point of its chart rather than a label on it, or a strip too narrow for the label size to sit in. A departure is named here so it stays a decision rather than becoming a drift.
typeScale.sheetNote: The two palette proof sheets under assets/color keep the earlier six-rung scale, because they are reading aids for the palette rather than chart deliveries and their density asked for finer steps.

gates.note: Every gate is computed once per theme, against that theme's own surface. A value that clears on paper has proved nothing about the dark ground, and the two runs print as separate lines.

ungated.rule: The gridline role is deliberately not gated. A gridline pushed to 3:1 competes with the data drawn over it, and it carries no information a reader has to recover. Structure that fails to read is a design defect, not an access barrier, so it is reviewed by eye rather than by ratio.

neutral.useWhen: The default, and the fallback whenever hue would carry no stable meaning. The series that carries the reading takes the hue; the steps behind it rank by lightness alone, starting with the value furthest from the ground. A figure never spends its data marks on the ink: a plot of ink-coloured marks with one accent is a plot that has given its only colour to the exception and none to the subject.

ordered.useWhen: The data is ordered: a value, a rank, a time position, a progress figure. One hue, five steps, and the step furthest from the ground reads as more.

categorical.useWhen: The categories are unordered and there are four or fewer. Five or more categories go neutral and carry labels.

derivation.note: What the palette owes the Style Reference it was derived from, in a form the corpus check can hold rather than a form a reader has to trust. Every role is in exactly one of the three lists below: it takes a reference token verbatim, it departs from one to clear a named gate, or it comes from an arithmetic the reference cannot carry.

kinds.ramp-interior: A rung between the ends of a magnitude ramp, placed by equal contrast rather than by mixing toward the ground. The ramp contract in palette-source holds its separation and its direction.
kinds.ink-at-alpha: That theme’s ink at a fixed alpha, computed rather than picked.

departures.why: Halo is the reference’s quietest grey and carries the fourth neutral step, which is a mark and owes the mark gate on white.

Ash reads as secondary text on white and is the natural fourth step on ink, where it sits under the mark gate until it is lightened. It moved twice: once for the reference ground, and again when the ground was warmed.

chosen.why: The reference grounds its dark theme on near-pure black, which reads harsh behind a card of figures. The shipped ground is warmed and lifted by the smallest amount that stops it reading as black, and every dark gate was recomputed against it: only the fourth neutral step had to move.
